target_customer: Cargo logistics operators and the US military for runway-free middle-mile delivery
problem: Long range cargo delivery needs fixed-wing efficiency but vertical takeoff and landing fits remote sites, and existing VTOL designs give up range.
business_model: Aircraft development funded by government contracts, with commercial cargo as the target
product_category: Electric cargo aircraft, eVTOL and drone systems

founders.name: Jamie Gull
education: Stanford, bachelor's and master's in aerospace engineering
founders.background_notes: YC page says aircraft design engineer at Scaled Composites and Falcon 9 aft thermal shield engineer at SpaceX.

founders.name: Evan Mucasey
founders.background_notes: The YC page gives no bio; the company site and press call both founders former SpaceX engineers.

exit.reason: Ampaire bought substantially all assets including eight patents and seven government contracts; terms not disclosed.

competitors.name: Sabrewing Aircraft
competitors.what: Gas-electric hybrid semi-autonomous regional cargo drone (Rhaegal)
competitors.funding_then: almost 2 million dollars from Drone Fund and others in March 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: A catch-in-midair electric fixed wing and winged drone system needs novel aircraft design, flight testing and certification pathways beyond a small team's normal reach.

defensibility.rationale: Eight patents and sole-source follow-on rights on seven government contracts gave some protection, though prototypes were still being tested.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it; Ampaire bought its assets in July 2023.

market_need_then: The US Air Force Agility Prime program funded eVTOL work, and the company's own site cites defense contracts as demand.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinct short name with trade press coverage of milestones, but no sourced brand identity or community.

outcome_analysis: Talyn built a long range electric cargo aircraft caught in midair by a winged drone and funded much of it through US Air Force programs. It sold substantially all assets, eight patents and seven government contracts, to Ampaire in July 2023, with the founders staying as advisors. The price was not disclosed and the reason for the sale was not stated, so failure_factors reflects a likely but unconfirmed capital constraint of a hardware company, and the outcome looks like an asset sale.
notes: Seed amounts of 1.5, 2.3 and 2.5 million dollars between 2020 and 2022, totals of 5.65 to 6.3 million, and a 1.7 million dollar AFWERX TACFI figure come only from aggregator snippets (Seedtable, Bouncewatch, PitchBook, FundedIQ) and conflict, so none is recorded as a round. The asset sale date and terms are from the search result summary of the Ampaire release; the article page itself returned HTTP 403. The Sabrewing source was found in an Elroy Air article search result; Elroy Air itself is dated 2021 so it is left out. The ran_out_of_money factor is an inference not stated by any source.
